small_guidance:
- Add more autotune configs sweeping BLOCK_HW ∈ {32, 64, 128, 256, 512} with BLOCK_OD also tunable (current BLOCK_OD=32 forces 32×BLOCK_HW accumulator regs — try smaller BLOCK_OD with an outer od-tile loop when OD is large; here OD=22 so BLOCK_OD=32 is OK but acc tile may be register-heavy).
- The conv has IC=3, KD=KH=KW=3 → 81 inner iters with full unroll potential. Reorder loops so kw/kh/kd are unrolled (constexpr trip counts already) and hoist `x_kh_base` arithmetic; consider precomputing `base_hw` as `(oh*W+ow)` once and reusing across kd/kh via constant offset additions in registers rather than recomputing offsets.
- Fuse the softmax into the conv-min kernel epilogue: have one program produce min for all OC at a given (n, oh, ow) tile, then do channel-softmax in registers — eliminates the second kernel launch and an HBM round-trip of the (N, OC, OH, OW) tensor.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as one program per (n, oh-tile, ow-tile) that computes the full OC=24 channel vector for that spatial tile, performs the min reduction over OD inline, and immediately runs channel-softmax in registers — single fused kernel, no intermediate write. With OC=24 (pad to 32) this fits comfortably in registers.
- Use an im2col-style GEMM view: treat (OC) × (IC*KD*KH*KW = 81) × (spatial tile) as a small GEMM per (n, od) slice; load the weight tile (OC=24, K=81) once into shared memory / registers and stream input patches. Combined with the OD-axis min reduction, this amortizes weight loads across all OD positions and all spatial tiles in the block.
- Consider doing the min reduction in an online fashion across od (keep running min in registers) so the per-od accumulator tile collapses from [BLOCK_OD, BLOCK_HW] to [BLOCK_HW], freeing registers for a larger BLOCK_HW or wider OC tile.
